parsed.headline: Voters scheduled to cast ballots in Toronto's 2026 municipal election

pages.text: According to the City of Toronto, voters are scheduled to head to the polls on a Monday for the 2026 municipal election. On election day, voting places will be open from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. While voting places close at 8 p.m., any voter in line by that time will be permitted to vote. To avoid lineups, the city suggests voters consider voting during off-peak hours between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.

Eligible voters must vote at their assigned voting place as indicated on their Voter Information Card (VIC) or the Toronto Elections webpage. To be eligible, a person must vote in the ward where they live, and may only vote once regardless of how many properties they own or rent in Toronto. To vote in person, individuals must show one piece of acceptable identification that includes their name and a qualifying Toronto address; photo identification is not required. The city encourages voters to bring their paper or digital VIC to facilitate a faster process. Voters on the voters' list can access their digital VIC and a list of acceptable identification at www.toronto.ca/Elections.

Voters may bring a friend, family member, caregiver, or other support person to assist them at the voting place. Individuals assisting a voter behind the voting screen are required to complete a declaration first. Alternatively, an election official can provide assistance to voters with accessibility needs.

parsed.headline: University of Ghana School of Law launches Supreme Court judgement review

pages.text: The University of Ghana School of Law (UGSoL) launched the “Ghana Supreme Court Review” on October 21, 2026, a publication designed to explain landmark decisions of the country's Supreme Court to the general public and outline their societal implications. Described as the first compendium of its kind in Ghana, the review was compiled by faculty members from the university and other faculties to provide context, explanation, and the legal basis for decisions made by the apex court. The publication is noted as being approximately four times the volume of a second book launched at the same event, titled “The Administrative Law in Ghana: Principles, practice and comparative perspectives.” This 800-page work contains 23 chapters and was produced with support from 14 contributors from the UGSoL, Pentecost University, and KAAF University law schools and faculties. During the launch event, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, the Vice-Chancellor of the university, stated that such authoritative works are necessary to ensure legal education and scholarships address the Ghanaian experience and contribute to national and global conversations. The event was attended by Chief Justice Justice Paul Baffor-Bonnie, other Supreme Court justices, law school deans, and students.

parsed.headline: US Embassy in Ottawa accuses Canadian officials of election meddling

pages.text: The US Embassy in Ottawa released a fact sheet on October 21, 2026, alleging that the Canadian government is meddling in the upcoming November US midterm elections. The embassy claimed that Canadian officials have brushed off concerns regarding potential interference and that ministers and premiers have openly described plans to influence American politics through public appearances and official documents. Specific actions cited by the embassy include meetings with US Democrats and calls for retaliatory tariffs against the US. The embassy noted that Industry Minister Mélanie Joly stated she was meeting with governors and potential presidential candidates in relation to tariff expectations if Democrats win the midterms. Additionally, the embassy alleged that Ontario Premier Doug Ford urged the Canadian federal government to consider retaliatory tariffs on imports from US states considered politically significant to the current administration's base of support.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford have denied allegations that the country is interfering in the US midterm elections. Responding to the claims on October 21, 2026, Carney stated that the US initiated trade actions against Canada first. He characterized the Canadian government's response as being in the interests of Canadian workers, families, and the economy to protect Canadian jobs and companies. The US midterms are scheduled for November and will determine which political party controls both branches of the US Congress.

parsed.headline: Armed UPDF members allegedly fire on tourists and law enforcement in Sajek, Bangladesh

pages.text: Armed members of the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF) allegedly opened fire on tourists and law enforcement personnel in the Gangaram Bazaar area of Sajek, Rangamati district, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR). The ISPR stated that approximately 30 to 40 rounds were fired at law enforcement and tourists around 11:00 AM on a Thursday. An army patrol team returned fire in self-defense and to ensure tourist safety, causing the armed individuals to flee the scene. No casualties were reported, and approximately 3,000 stranded tourists were subsequently evacuated safely to Khagrachari through coordinated efforts by the Bangladesh Army and police. The ISPR described the violence and blockade as apparently premeditated, alleging that the UPDF forcibly used local residents as human shields and coerced them into participating in the blockade. The statement noted that a faction of armed UPDF members had taken positions in the tourist area following ongoing security operations in parts of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

parsed.headline: Yelloway research collaboration develops fully fertile Cavendish banana

pages.text: Yelloway, a research collaboration between the banana company Chiquita and crop-improvement company KeyGene, announced this month that it has developed a fully fertile Cavendish banana. Because Cavendish bananas typically have three sets of chromosomes, they are usually sterile. The development of a fertile version may allow for cross-breeding to create new, commercially viable banana varieties that are resistant to disease. This follows reports of threats to the Cavendish, which is the variety most commonly found in global fruit bowls. Dr. Jose De Vega, an expert on crop genomics at the Earlham Institute in Norwich, noted that the Cavendish is under threat from diseases including Tropical Race 4 (TR4), a strain of Panama disease that has spread from Southeast Asia to Australia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America. De Vega cited a December 2025 report from Ecuador, the world's largest banana exporter, as a particularly worrying development regarding the disease. The threat to banana varieties impacts global supply chains and the food security of millions in the tropics who rely on bananas and plantains as a staple food and source of income. Globally, approximately 139 million tonnes of bananas are grown annually, making them the second most consumed fruit after the tomato.

parsed.headline: U.S. and Israel planning for possible attack on Iran, source tells NPR

pages.text: The United States and Israel are preparing plans for a possible attack on Iran in early November, following the U.S. midterm elections, according to a person briefed on war planning who spoke to NPR on Thursday. The source, who requested anonymity to discuss the preparations, stated that the U.S. is currently amassing forces in the region to be ready for an attack by early November, though these preparations could also serve as part of a campaign to pressure Iran into a diplomatic deal. 10/22/2026. According to the source, Israel had initially planned to strike Iran in mid-October, approximately two weeks before the Israeli elections on Oct. 27, but President Trump objected to that timing.

In response to the reported planning, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Iranian state media on Thursday that the country is prepared for both diplomacy and war, stating that any scenario is conceivable, including an attack by the U.S. and Israel. Iranian state media also cited a security source claiming that if Iranian officials or civilian infrastructure are attacked, Iran would retaliate by targeting U.S. interests in the region, as well as the assets and infrastructure of countries participating in the war. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is seeking reelection, is campaigning on a threat to topple the Iranian regime.
